what: When the mouse passes over a photo, water clings to the spot (radius .004 · amount 3.5), is pushed in the direction the hand moved (1.6, up to speed 4) and flows, blends with neighbors (.79), shrinks at a rate of 1.5 per second (friction 3), and the edges ripple with fine noise (2.6 · grain .7). Where depth exceeds .395 is water, and the surface slope adds a top-left glint and edge shade. Spots that passed depth .2~.4 remain as marks and dry over 3 seconds. On the photo cell If there is one, the photo under the water refracts, if not, only gloss and shade are laid on as a transparent film. On devices without WebGL2 + half-precision support, with fingers, or with reduced motion, it does nothing. Stops drawing once fully dry · look: reveal shows another picture (a photo with flowers arranged) showing through where the hand passed instead of water, then fading away

options.push: Push strength scaled to hand speed, default 1.6
options.dry: Seconds for marks to dry, default 3
options.[data-fx-part=photo]: Photo slot to lay the water over (inside if present, refract). If absent, the element itself
options.look: If reveal, a “show-through” replaces water — only where the hand has passed (water depth .05 to edge+.25 smoothed) [data-fx-part=Inside reveal] (e.g. the same photo with flowers in it) shows through as the water recedes and then vanishes. With no image, a bright light halo (--fx-water-light, alpha .55)
options.[data-fx-part=reveal]: look: image revealed in reveal (a child holding )

from.where: index.html .co-card.is-soon (coming-soon collection photo) — original OGL water version (short 512 · radius .004 · amount 3.5 · push 1.6 · friction 3 · spread .79 · decay 1.5 · wobble 2.6 · grain .7 · threshold .395 · dry 3 · mark .2 to .4), turns on in sequence over .3s on hover
index.html .hero (Hero — over a photo of a vase without flowers, the photo with flowers shows through only where the pointer has passed, original hero vase-bare · vase-flowers · flower-mask)

note: Required library: library/_vendor/ogl@1.0.11/ogl.min.js (global OGL). Of the original’s several looks, such as dew and milk marks, only the water mark was carried over.
